# origincloud_network_acl_rule (Resource)

An ACL rule: accepts or drops the traffic it matches in one direction.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `acl` (String) The acl the acl rule is in. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `action` (String) What the rule does with the traffic it matches. One of `ACCEPT`, `DROP`. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `cidr_block` (String) The far side's range: where entering traffic comes from, or where leaving traffic goes to. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `direction` (String) Which traffic the rule applies to. One of `INGRESS`, `EGRESS`. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `priority` (Number) The rule's place in its direction, from 1; lower comes first. No two rules of a direction share one. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `project` (String) The project the acl rule is in. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `protocol` (String) The traffic the rule matches. One of `ALL`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMP`. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `region` (String) The region the acl rule is in. Changing it replaces the acl rule.

### Optional

- `first_port` (Number) The first port the rule matches, for `TCP` and `UDP`. Each set of ports has one spelling, and the rule reads back in it: `first_port` 0 and `last_port` 0 match every port, a `last_port` of 0 the single port `first_port`, and a `first_port` below `last_port` the range between them. Any other spelling of a set is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the one to use: `first_port` 22 and `last_port` 22 is `first_port` 22 and `last_port` 0, and 0 or 1 to 65535 is 0 and 0. Changing it replaces the acl rule.
- `last_port` (Number) The last port the rule matches, above `first_port`; 0 for the single port `first_port`, or with `first_port` 0 for every port. Changing it replaces the acl rule.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The acl rule's resource name, the same as `name`.
- `name` (String) The rule's resource name.
